moduleTitle: Configuring and managing projects in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Explain the process of generating base test code using the command line interface (CLI) to streamline test execution.
Describe how to manage project users, invite teammates, and assign roles to ensure smooth team collaboration.
Explain how to oversee projects and users at the company level, managing multiple projects and teammates efficiently.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Generating base test code with the CLI

elements.description: Settings > CLI generates a base command with token/project ID for a CI integration or local shell. Select platform/grid where applicable. CLI access depends on the subscription; a local initiating shell is distinct from the target execution infrastructure.
Copy the base command, then configure a supported runtime, connectivity, selected tests/grid and appropriate secret handling. Generated text alone does not establish execution readiness.

bulletPoints: Generate a CI/local-shell base command; configure execution prerequisites before running.
Keep generated credentials out of public logs and source control.

elements.description: The Project teammates screen (via the Users icon in the main navigation) lists everyone currently assigned to the project. Inviting is done by entering each teammate's work email (followed by space or Enter), then clicking Invite.

Project members can invite teammates; project owners can remove teammates and change project ownership. Removing a teammate from a project does not remove them from the company. The sole project owner cannot be removed.

bulletPoints: Invite teammates: Users icon → enter work email(s) → Invite.
Any member can invite; only an owner can remove teammates or add/remove other owners.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Overseeing projects and users at the company level

elements.description: Company administration lists projects and teammates; invitations grant access only to projects the inviter can access. Membership does not describe every action. The professional-plan Audit Log, restricted to project/company owners, records user, action and time and offers project/member/action filters.

elements.text: Dashboard Recent Activity can also expose events within its scope. External issue/TMS integrations are not a required substitute for the built-in Audit Log. Company owners manage company ownership, and the last company owner must remain.

bulletPoints: Project membership, company administration and event audit are different views.
Audit Log requires the appropriate plan and owner access.
Invitations do not confer access to projects the inviter cannot access.

elements.description: A toggle in the project's pull request settings that prevents writing directly to the Master branch and/or other selected branches (making them read-only) — changes must go through a pull request instead of a direct commit.

If Master is protected, 'Allow Auto-improve on master' can still be enabled so the Auto-improve locator feature keeps working even on a protected branch. 'Require approving reviewer' can be turned on per-branch to mandate a review before a pull request merges. Only the project owner or company owner can change these settings, and they're a professional-plan-only feature.

bulletPoints: Protect Master from changes = prevents direct writes to Master (and/or other selected branches) — changes must go through a PR.
Allow Auto-improve on master: keeps Auto-improve working even when Master is protected.
Only project/company owners can configure this; professional plan only.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming any team member can remove another teammate
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Expecting a regular project member to be able to remove someone from the project the same way they can invite someone.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inviting is open to any team member, but removing teammates or adding/removing project owners is restricted to project owners.

examPitfalls.title: Treating generated CLI code as complete execution setup
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming copied code installs the runtime, provisions a grid and safely stores its token.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Generate a base command, then configure runtime, target infrastructure, tests and secrets.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing membership with actions
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating project membership as a record of actions, or requiring an external tracker for all activity visibility.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use membership views for access and the owner-only professional-plan Audit Log for user/action/time records; Dashboard activity is a separate scoped view.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing 'Protect Master from changes' with deleting or locking out all edits
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming the protection setting deletes the master branch or makes it completely uneditable by anyone under any circumstance.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: It only prevents direct writes — changes still happen through pull requests, and Auto-improve can still be allowed to run against a protected master if that toggle is enabled.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Who can remove a teammate from the project in Testim?
practiceQuiz.hint: Inviting and removing are different permission levels.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Project owners can remove project teammates; the sole owner cannot be removed. Project removal does not imply company removal.

optionExplanations.A: Invitation authority is not removal authority.
optionExplanations.B: Project owners have documented removal authority, except for the sole owner.
optionExplanations.C: Regular membership alone does not grant removal authority.
optionExplanations.D: Read-only observation does not grant project-owner removal authority.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How can you run your tests using the CLI in Testim?

options.text: By executing tests directly from the Testim dashboard
By integrating tests with your continuous integration (CI) platform or using your local shell
By using only the CI Integration option
By downloading a separate Testim CLI application

practiceQuiz.hint: A supported CLI can be initiated from a local shell or CI runner.
practiceQuiz.rationale: CI runners and local shells can invoke the npm CLI after prerequisites are configured. Generated base commands do not install the runtime or provision execution infrastructure.

optionExplanations.A: Dashboard interaction is not itself a CLI invocation.
optionExplanations.B: A configured local shell or CI runner can invoke the CLI.
optionExplanations.C: CLI execution is not restricted to CI.
optionExplanations.D: The documented runtime is the npm package, not a separate standalone app.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO statements correctly distinguish membership management from activity inspection in Testim?

options.text: Project teammates and company administration expose user/project membership.
Inviting a user grants access to any project, including projects the inviter cannot access.
Every user can inspect all company audit events without plan or role restrictions.
Authorized owners on the professional plan can inspect user/action/time records in the Audit Log.

practiceQuiz.hint: Membership and an authorized event log answer different questions.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Membership views identify project associations. The built-in Audit Log records actions and users with owner/plan restrictions; an external project-management tool is not universally required.

optionExplanations.A: These administration views expose membership associations.
optionExplanations.B: An invitation cannot grant project access beyond the inviter’s access.
optionExplanations.C: The Audit Log has plan and owner restrictions.
optionExplanations.D: Authorized owners can inspect built-in action records.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does the "Protect Master from changes" setting do in Testim's pull requests settings?

options.text: Allows changes to the master branch
Prevents writing directly to the master branch
Makes the master branch editable by all users

practiceQuiz.hint: It's a branch-protection toggle, like read-only mode.
practiceQuiz.rationale: 'Protect branches from changes' (applied here to Master) prevents writing directly to that branch — changes must go through a pull request instead. It doesn't allow direct edits, delete anything, or open the branch up to all users.

optionExplanations.A: Protection restricts direct changes rather than enabling them.
optionExplanations.B: Read-only protection prevents direct writes; use the configured PR workflow.
optionExplanations.C: Protection does not delete the branch.
optionExplanations.D: Protection does not give everyone edit access.

quickRecap.value: Settings > CLI generates a base command; runtime, credentials and target execution infrastructure still need configuration.
Users icon → work email(s) → Invite (any team member can do this).
Project-owner permission; sole owner cannot be removed. Project removal does not remove company membership.
Separate project/company membership from owner-only professional-plan Audit Log records and scoped Dashboard activity.
Prevents direct writes to Master; changes go through a PR. Owner-only, professional plan.
